$schema_note: Timber species reference for staircase design. Values are typical ranges — actual density and hardness vary by growth region, age, moisture content. Cost bands are relative UK indicators (£ = economy, £££££ = premium), not absolute prices.

species.name: European oak
species.notes: Warm tone, prominent grain, medullary rays; the UK default premium timber.

species.name: American white oak
species.notes: Cleaner, straighter grain than European oak; paler tone; often preferred for modern designs.

species.name: Walnut (generic)
species.notes: Rich chocolate tone with darker striping; premium feature timber.

species.name: American walnut
species.notes: The premium walnut spec — one of the finest luxury staircase timbers.

species.name: Ash
species.notes: Pale cream tone, open straight grain, close to oak in hardness; suits bright modern interiors.

species.name: Hard (rock) maple
species.notes: Very pale, fine smooth grain; harder than oak; can yellow under UV.

species.name: American cherry
species.notes: Warm pinkish-brown ageing to deep red-brown; softer than oak.

species.name: European beech
species.notes: Pale cream, fine grain; moves more than oak so needs good moisture control.

species.name: Sapele
species.notes: Reddish-brown African hardwood; often used where genuine mahogany would be specified.

species.name: Iroko
species.notes: Yellow-brown darkening with age; dense, durable, teak-like.

species.name: Idigbo
species.notes: Pale yellow, straight grain; economical alternative to oak for painted work.

species.name: American tulipwood
species.notes: Very pale green-tinged; classic 'paint-grade hardwood'; smooth finish under paint.

species.name: Scandinavian pine
species.notes: The UK default painted-staircase timber; economical, works well painted.

species.name: White deal (pine)
species.notes: Trade term for painted-grade softwood used in staircase carcasses.

species.name: Hemlock
species.notes: Pale, straight-grained; sometimes used as alternative to pine.

species.name: Douglas fir
species.notes: Warm reddish tone; harder than pine; used for structural + visible components.

species.name: Accoya (modified)
species.notes: Chemically-modified radiata pine; extreme dimensional stability; expensive for what it is on interior work.

species.name: Genuine mahogany
species.notes: CITES-restricted; most modern 'mahogany' is sapele/sipo/utile. Genuine Swietenia rare and premium.
